name: Oppression
momentumNotes: Resources feel compressed; inner truth and endurance matter while outer options are limited.
theme: Oppression is the feeling of water trapped beneath the lake. Outer resources may be thin, but inner truth can still remain unbroken.
basicInterpretation: When expression is limited, guard the dignity of your inner voice. Reduce waste, speak simply, and do not abandon what is true because it is hard.
reflectionPrompt: What remains honest in you when support is scarce?

reversed.theme: Flipped upside down, Oppression becomes Hexagram 48, The Well. This other side brings in the atmosphere of source, nourishment, tradition, asking how the situation may look from another threshold.
reversed.reflection: Let The Well widen the reading rather than replace it. Consider what another person, timing, or hidden part of you might see when the pattern is viewed from the far side.
reversed.applicationPrompt: Visualize your question from the far side, as if another person or your future self is looking back through The Well. Notice where source, nourishment, tradition and a sustaining, renewing movement reveal needs, timing, or motives that the first view may miss.

opposite.theme: The contrast to Oppression is Hexagram 22, Grace. Where the primary pattern emphasizes confinement, exhaustion, truth under pressure, this complementary field points toward beauty, adornment, form.
opposite.reflection: This is not the main movement of the reading, but it shows what balances or challenges it. It can also highlight hidden causes or contrasting forces at play. Notice where Grace names the medicine, shadow, or unchosen path beside the situation.
opposite.applicationPrompt: Visualize Grace as the contrasting color laid beside Oppression. Ask what hidden cause, missing medicine, or opposing pressure is suggested by beauty, adornment, form, especially where the situation carries a supportive, restrained tone.
